chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayn, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man intends to marry a woman, let him say, 'I affirm the Covenant which Allah took: to keep [them] in good fellowship or to let [them] go with kindness.'

key_terms.الْمِيثَاقِ: The Covenant (referring to the marital bond)

ai.seo_question: What should a man say when he intends to marry a woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, prescribing a specific declaration of the marital covenant (mithaq) upon the intention of marriage. This supplication explicitly invokes the Quranic principle of 'holding onto in kindness or releasing with grace,' grounding the legal status of marriage in divine covenant rather than mere contract. It highlights the Shia emphasis on spiritual mindfulness and ethical conduct as the foundation of marital rights and duties.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Ayn who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Whenever the man intends to get marry the woman, so let him say, ‘I accept with the Covenant which Allahazwj has Taken [2:229] then keep (them) in good fellowship or let (them) go with kindness’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Aban from ‘Abd af-Rahman ibn ‘ A‘yan who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
When a man wants to marry a woman he should say, “I authenticate my covenant with Allah which is: “maintain in a reasonable way or allow to go with kindness.” [2:229]’”
